POSITIVE_CONTROL_SYNTHETIC_SPA.description: Synthetic deterministic SPA with 8 states, 4 actions, known action->next-state mapping

NULL_CONTROL_SHUFFLED_ACTIONS.description: Shuffled-action permutation test within sessions: destroys action->next_url association

NULL_CONTROL_NORMALIZED_URL.description: Normalized URL PMI (fragment-stripped) at K=0 with alpha=0

observations: K=3 conditional PMI is exactly 0.0 bits on ALL 5 TodoMVC hash-SPA variants. This is a deterministic consequence: on these minimal deterministic SPAs with 3-4 hash states and K=3 action history, the (url_before, H_K=3) stratum fully determines url_after, making I(url_after; action | url_before, H_K=3) = 0 by mathematical identity.

K=1 conditional PMI is 0.074-0.081 bits but permutation p-values (0.11-0.33) are NOT significant after Bonferroni correction (alpha=0.01). The residual PMI at K=1 is consistent with partial state determination by 1-step history.
K=0 unconditional PMI reproduces parent signal exactly: 0.187-0.204 bits with Bonferroni p=0.001 on all 5 variants. This validates data reuse and pipeline consistency.
Action-history prediction accuracy at K=3 is 100% on 4/5 variants and 95.4% on vue, confirming that (url_before, H_K=3) fully determines url_after on these deterministic SPAs.
Positive control passes: synthetic 8-state deterministic SPA achieves PMI=1.496 bits at K=3 with p=0.001, validating the PMI pipeline detects known structure.
Normalized URL PMI (fragment-stripped) is exactly 0.0 bits with alpha=0, confirming fragment information is the sole PMI source.
The K=1 to K=3 PMI drop (0.074 -> 0.0 bits) quantifies the Markov information loss: 1-step history captures ~60% of the unconditional PMI, and 3-step history captures 100%.
validity_notes: The K=3 PMI=0.0 result is mathematically forced on TodoMVC hash-SPAs because these are deterministic FSMs with 3-4 states. With K=3 previous actions, the (url_before, H_K=3) stratum uniquely identifies the current FSM state, making the next URL fully determined regardless of the current action.

The parent's 0.188-0.209 bit unconditional PMI signal is entirely explained by Markov predictability: (url_before, action) -> url_after is deterministic on these SPAs, so I(url_after; action | url_before) > 0 is trivially true.
The K=1 permutation p-values are not significant, suggesting the K=1 PMI (0.074 bits) may partly reflect estimator noise or small-sample effects rather than genuine beyond-Markov structure.

This experiment tests only TodoMVC hash-SPAs with 3-4 states. The result does not generalize to production SPAs with larger state spaces, stochastic transitions, or history-based routing where H_K=3 may not fully determine the FSM state.
Data reuse from parent EXP-PHYSICS-35209110569. No new browser collection. Integrity relies on parent file hashes.
The frozen decision rule's falsification threshold (K=3 PMI > 0.05 on >=3/5 variants) is decisively failed: 0/5 variants achieve any positive PMI at K=3.
unresolved: Whether production SPAs with larger state spaces (>4 states) and stochastic transitions exhibit beyond-Markov PMI structure at K=3 or higher. TodoMVC is too minimal to test this.
Whether the K=1 residual PMI (0.074 bits, p=0.11-0.33) would become significant with larger sample sizes or more SPA variants. Current power may be insufficient.
Whether richer state representations (DOM, accessibility tree, visual layout) on TodoMVC or production SPAs would reveal beyond-Markov structure not visible at the URL level.
Whether stochastic SPAs (e.g., with auth, pagination, user-dependent content) where H_K=3 does NOT fully determine the next state would show positive K=3 PMI.
